facts.claim: Official Python SDK exists; repo holds SDK plus a walkthrough notebook
facts.quote: This repository holds the Python SDK for the Unbox AI API and a notebook that walks through the model step by step.

facts.claim: Widgets use a publishable key so the secret key stays off pages and apps
facts.quote: On a page or in an app, where your API key must never go, the widgets make the same calls with a publishable key.

facts.claim: MCP server exists and shares naming with portal JSON and widgets (no tool list found)
facts.quote: The portal's JSON uses the same names (catalog_id, user_id, user, item_id, item_ids), as do the widgets and the MCP server.

facts.claim: Model can only return items in a catalog it knows; the action vocabulary is the uploaded catalog
facts.quote: The model can only return items it knows about (a history can still hold items outside your catalogs).

facts.claim: Items need not be products; artworks used as proof (title as name, artist as brand, views for sales)
facts.quote: Embedding and every query work the same at any size; only the map is skipped.

facts.claim: Catalog upload needs at least id, name, event_type=product, group=product; rest may be null (title-only embedding). Quote is a related limit.
facts.quote: If none of the first 500 fetched images can be used, the job fails instead of embedding text only.

facts.claim: Each API key holds 2 catalogs; third upload refused until one is deleted
facts.quote: Once both slots are in use, an upload under a new name is refused until you delete one of them.
`client.umap(catalog_ids=[...])` draws one map of several catalogs instead, one colour each, at most 5 of them.

facts.claim: Key shown on screen at signup and emailed; new key or catalog upload via portal login with same email
facts.quote: To get a new key or upload your own catalog, sign in at portal.unboxai.com with the same email.

facts.claim: Full catalog ranked in one forward pass (latency claim)
facts.quote: BehaviorGPT reads the event sequence directly and ranks a whole catalogue in one forward pass.

facts.claim: Terms permit rate limiting and key revocation; no numeric limit published
facts.quote: We may limit how many requests a key makes, and we may revoke a key that is misused.

facts.claim: Terms: API keys are server-side only
facts.quote: Keep API keys secret: use them only on your servers, never in a page or an app.

facts.claim: Terms: acceptable use bars harm, deception, tracking or discrimination of people (matters for manipulation-style demos)
facts.quote: use the Services against the law, or to harm, deceive, track or discriminate against people;

facts.claim: Anomaly-detection app scores each shopping session step with no labels; flags risk barrier crossing
facts.quote: It flags the step where a session crosses a calibrated risk barrier and names the items that pushed it there.

facts.claim: Art recommender demo uses 19,000 public-domain artworks with BehaviorGPT as curator
facts.quote: Browse 19,000 public-domain artworks from the Art Institute of Chicago with BehaviorGPT as the curator.

facts.claim: v4 benchmark claim: 30 of 31 dataset-task pairs zero-shot, sub-millisecond catalog ranking
facts.quote: leads on 30 of 31 dataset–task pairs zero-shot, and ranks a full catalog in under a millisecond per query.

facts.claim: Company zero-shot claim vs baselines trained on up to 2.7M samples
facts.quote: Zero-shot, it beats every baseline trained on up to 2.7 million samples of the target data.

facts.claim: Company claims double-digit sales lift in production A/B tests; no customers named
facts.quote: In production A/B tests, BehaviorGPT models have increased sales by double-digit percentages against incumbent systems.
